findings.section: 1. How often each side resigns, and from what

findings.section: 1. How often each side resigns, and from what
findings.claim: In bullet about three in ten of the player's resignations came from positions the model still rated P(win) >= 0.2, the same as for the opponents.
findings.metric: share of the side's resignations whose resignation position had calibrated model P(win) >= 0.2 from the resigner's view (position after the last move, flipped to the resigner when the opponent moved last)
findings.caveat: Model probabilities are model-relative (the pooled calibrated model is under-confident at the extremes); see section 3 for the empirical check.

findings.section: 1. How often each side resigns, and from what
findings.claim: In blitz the player resigns from positions the model still rated P(win) >= 0.2 somewhat more often than the opponents do.
findings.metric: share of the side's resignations whose resignation position had calibrated model P(win) >= 0.2 from the resigner's view
findings.caveat: Model probabilities are model-relative; no paired difference is printed for this row.

findings.section: 1. How often each side resigns, and from what
findings.claim: In rapid the player resigns from positions the model still rated P(win) >= 0.2 more than twice as often as the opponents do.
findings.metric: share of the side's resignations whose resignation position had calibrated model P(win) >= 0.2 from the resigner's view
findings.caveat: Model probabilities are model-relative; no paired difference is printed for this row.

findings.section: 1. How often each side resigns, and from what

findings.metric: share of the side's resignations whose resignation position had calibrated model P(win) >= 0.1 from the resigner's view
findings.caveat: Model probabilities are model-relative.

findings.section: 1. How often each side resigns, and from what

findings.metric: share of the side's resignations whose resignation position had calibrated model P(win) >= 0.1 from the resigner's view
findings.caveat: Model probabilities are model-relative.

findings.section: 1. How often each side resigns, and from what

findings.metric: share of the side's resignations whose resignation position had calibrated model P(win) >= 0.1 from the resigner's view
findings.caveat: Model probabilities are model-relative.

findings.section: 1. How often each side resigns, and from what
findings.claim: The median resignation position in bullet is worth about 0.15 expected points to the player by the model, slightly more than for the opponents.
findings.metric: median calibrated model EV = P(win) + 0.5 P(draw) at the resignation position, resigner's view
findings.caveat: Model-relative; no CI printed.

findings.section: 1. How often each side resigns, and from what
findings.claim: The median resignation position in blitz is worth about 0.12 expected points to the player by the model, slightly more than for the opponents.
findings.metric: median calibrated model EV = P(win) + 0.5 P(draw) at the resignation position, resigner's view
findings.caveat: Model-relative; no CI printed.

findings.section: 1. How often each side resigns, and from what
findings.claim: The median resignation position in rapid is worth about twice as much to the player by the model as the opponents' median resignation position is to them.
findings.metric: median calibrated model EV = P(win) + 0.5 P(draw) at the resignation position, resigner's view
findings.caveat: Model-relative; no CI printed.

findings.section: 1. How often each side resigns, and from what
findings.claim: The player resigned during the opponent's turn (having moved last) in about a fifth of resignations, more often than the opponents did.
findings.metric: share of the side's resignations in which the resigner made the last recorded move of the game

findings.section: 1. How often each side resigns, and from what
findings.claim: The median engine evaluation at the player's resignations is about -6.4 pawns from the player's side, less hopeless than at the opponents' resignations.
findings.metric: median Stockfish eval (cp) at the resignation position from the resigner's side

findings.section: 1. How often each side resigns, and from what
findings.claim: About one resignation in thirteen, for both sides, happened with the engine eval better than -300 cp for the resigner.
findings.metric: share of the side's resignations with engine eval better than -300 cp from the resigner's side

findings.section: 1. How often each side resigns, and from what
findings.claim: The player resigned 22 games (2.8% of resignations) from positions that were level or better on the board; the opponents resigned 30 such games.
findings.metric: number of the side's resignations with engine eval >= 0 from the resigner's side

findings.section: 2. Expected points given away by resigning, model view
findings.claim: By the calibrated model, each bullet resignation gave away about 0.18 expected points, slightly less than the opponents' resignations handed over.
findings.metric: mean calibrated model EV at the resignation position from the resigner's view, per resigned game (bootstrap over resigned games)
findings.stake_note: Total model EV of the player's resignations (41.5 [37.1, 45.8] points) spread over every bullet game; about 8 Elo of expected score.
findings.caveat: Model view only: the model is under-confident at the extremes and was fitted on all games including the resigned ones; section 3's played-out comparison is the robust estimate.

findings.section: 2. Expected points given away by resigning, model view
findings.claim: By the calibrated model, each blitz resignation gave away about 0.16 expected points, slightly more than the opponents' resignations handed over.
findings.metric: mean calibrated model EV at the resignation position from the resigner's view, per resigned game (bootstrap over resigned games)
findings.stake_note: Total model EV of the player's resignations (63.5 [58.5, 68.5] points) spread over every blitz game; about 22 Elo of expected score.
findings.caveat: Model view only; section 3's played-out comparison is the robust estimate.

findings.section: 2. Expected points given away by resigning, model view
findings.claim: By the calibrated model, each rapid resignation gave away about 0.17 expected points, markedly more than the opponents' resignations handed over.
findings.metric: mean calibrated model EV at the resignation position from the resigner's view, per resigned game (bootstrap over resigned games)
findings.stake_note: Total model EV of the player's resignations (27.5 [23.8, 31.4] points) spread over every rapid game; about 32 Elo of expected score.
findings.caveat: Model view only; section 3's played-out comparison is the robust estimate.

findings.section: 3. The empirical check
findings.claim: Valued at how the player's own played-out games from the same model-EV bins actually ended, each bullet resignation cost about 0.16 points, the same as the opponents' resignations handed over.
findings.metric: mean played-out score (win 1, draw 0.5) of the resigner's EV bin, same side and time class, per resignation; joint bootstrap over comparison games and resigned games
findings.stake_note: Played-out total of the player's bullet resignations (37.2 [31.2, 43.1] points; all-positions lower bound 35.4) spread over all 3453 bullet games; about 7 Elo of expected score.
findings.caveat: Comparison positions come from games the side did not resign or abandon, which are themselves selected (upper-ish bound); positions weighted per position, CIs clustered by game.

findings.section: 3. The empirical check
findings.claim: Valued at how played-out games from the same model-EV bins actually ended, each blitz resignation cost the player about 0.14 points, more than the opponents' resignations handed over.
findings.metric: mean played-out score of the resigner's EV bin, same side and time class, per resignation; joint bootstrap over comparison games and resigned games
findings.stake_note: Played-out total of the player's blitz resignations (57.5 [48.9, 66.7] points; all-positions lower bound 44.8) spread over all 1987 blitz games; about 20 Elo of expected score.
findings.caveat: Comparison positions come from games the side did not resign or abandon (upper-ish bound); CIs clustered by game.

findings.section: 3. The empirical check
findings.claim: Valued at how played-out games from the same model-EV bins actually ended, each rapid resignation cost the player about 0.23 points, three times what the opponents' resignations handed over.
findings.metric: mean played-out score of the resigner's EV bin, same side and time class, per resignation; joint bootstrap over comparison games and resigned games
findings.stake_note: Played-out total of the player's rapid resignations (36.4 [27.7, 46.0] points; all-positions lower bound 23.9) spread over all 589 rapid games; about 43 Elo of expected score.
findings.caveat: Rapid has only 589 games and 162 player resignations, so bin rates are wide; comparison set is an upper-ish bound.

findings.section: 3. The empirical check
findings.claim: Over all time classes the player's 788 resignations gave away about 131 expected points on the played-out valuation and the opponents' 809 resignations handed over about 97, a net cost of 34 points over 6,029 games.
findings.metric: sum over resignations of the played-out score of the resignation's EV bin (same side, same time class); net = opponents' total minus player's total
findings.stake_note: Played-out valuation; the model valuation gives 132 and the all-positions lower bound 104; roughly 15 Elo of expected score (2.2 points per 100 games).
findings.caveat: Played-out comparison set is an upper-ish bound (non-resigned games are selected); the model view is the lower-ish bound.

findings.section: 3. The empirical check
findings.claim: Pooled over time classes each of the player's resignations cost about 0.17 expected points on the played-out valuation, against 0.12 handed over per opponent resignation.
findings.metric: played-out total divided by the number of resignations, pooled over time classes
findings.stake_note: 131 points spread over all 6,029 games; roughly 15 Elo of expected score.
findings.caveat: No CI printed for the pooled figure; see the per-time-class rows.

findings.section: 3. The empirical check
findings.claim: In bullet, positions the model valued at 0.20-0.30 scored 0.21 when the player played them out, more than the same positions scored for the opponents.
findings.metric: observed score (win 1, draw 0.5) of positions in the side's played-out games with model EV 0.20-0.30 from that side's view; CIs clustered by game
findings.caveat: Positions weighted per position (long slides count more); games that were played out are selected.

findings.section: 3. The empirical check
findings.claim: In rapid, positions the model valued at 0.10-0.15 scored 0.19 when the player played them out, five times what the same positions scored for the opponents.
findings.metric: observed score of positions in the side's played-out games with model EV 0.10-0.15 from that side's view; CIs clustered by game
findings.n: 427 (97) player positions (games), 660 (110) opponent positions; 24 player resignations in this bin
findings.caveat: Rapid bin rates are wide (589 games).

findings.section: 4. The clock
findings.claim: Only 1% of the player's bullet resignations happened with the opponent under 10 s, against 6% of the opponents' resignations; 82% happened with the opponent at 30 s or more.
findings.metric: share of the side's bullet resignations with the other side's clock under 10 s at the resignation position
findings.caveat: Clock at the position after the last recorded move; the time between that move and the resignation is not recorded.

findings.section: 4. The clock
findings.claim: Most of the player's bullet resignations happened with the opponent at 30 s or more, a larger share than for the opponents' resignations.
findings.metric: share of the side's bullet resignations with the other side's clock >= 30 s at the resignation position

findings.section: 4. The clock
findings.claim: Almost all blitz resignations by either side happened with the other side at 30 s or more.
findings.metric: share of the side's blitz resignations with the other side's clock >= 30 s at the resignation position

findings.section: 6. Rule of thumb in engine terms
findings.claim: In bullet, positions with mate against the player or eval <= -2000 scored 0.32 when played out with the opponent under 10 s, against 0.09 with the opponent at 30 s or more.
findings.metric: observed score of the player's positions in played-out bullet games with engine eval mate / <= -2000 from the player's side and the opponent's clock under 10 s; baseline is the same cell with the opponent at >= 30 s (0.093 [0.064, 0.127])
findings.caveat: Played-out games are selected (a player who did not resign may have had a reason such as the opponent's clock); positions weighted per position.

findings.section: 6. Rule of thumb in engine terms
findings.claim: In bullet, positions at -1000..-500 (roughly a rook down) scored 0.60 for the player when played out with the opponent under 10 s, against 0.28 with the opponent at 30 s or more.
findings.metric: observed score of the player's positions in played-out bullet games with engine eval -1000..-500 from the player's side and the opponent's clock under 10 s; baseline is the same cell with the opponent at >= 30 s (0.279 [0.244, 0.314])
findings.caveat: Played-out games are selected; positions weighted per position.

findings.section: 6. Rule of thumb in engine terms
findings.claim: In bullet, positions with mate against or eval <= -2000 still scored 0.20 when the player played them out, and 0.17 for the opponents.
findings.metric: observed score of positions in the side's played-out games with engine eval mate / <= -2000 from that side's view; CIs clustered by game
findings.n: 10,884 (1199) player positions (games), 10,751 (953) opponent positions; 30 player resignations in this cell
findings.caveat: Played-out games are selected; positions weighted per position.

findings.section: 6. Rule of thumb in engine terms
findings.claim: In blitz, positions with mate against or eval <= -2000 scored 0.08 when played out, identically for the player and the opponents.
findings.metric: observed score of positions in the side's played-out games with engine eval mate / <= -2000 from that side's view; CIs clustered by game
findings.n: 5,717 (470) player positions (games), 5,263 (415) opponent positions; 49 player resignations in this cell
findings.caveat: Played-out games are selected; positions weighted per position.

findings.section: 6. Rule of thumb in engine terms
findings.claim: In rapid, positions with mate against or eval <= -2000 scored 0.12 when the player played them out, four times what they scored for the opponents.
findings.metric: observed score of positions in the side's played-out games with engine eval mate / <= -2000 from that side's view; CIs clustered by game
findings.n: 1,108 (101) player positions (games), 1,515 (131) opponent positions; 18 player resignations in this cell
findings.caveat: Rapid has few games; played-out games are selected.

findings.section: 6. Rule of thumb in engine terms
findings.claim: In bullet, positions at -1000..-500 (roughly a rook down) scored 0.37 when the player played them out; this is the eval band where most of the player's bullet resignations happened.
findings.metric: observed score of positions in the side's played-out games with engine eval -1000..-500 from that side's view; CIs clustered by game
findings.n: 21,882 (1627) player positions (games), 25,195 (1596) opponent positions; 138 player resignations in this cell
findings.caveat: Played-out games are selected; positions weighted per position.

findings.section: 6. Rule of thumb in engine terms
findings.claim: In blitz, positions at -1000..-500 scored 0.23 when the player played them out, slightly less than for the opponents; most of the player's blitz resignations fall in this eval band.
findings.metric: observed score of positions in the side's played-out games with engine eval -1000..-500 from that side's view; CIs clustered by game
findings.n: 7,129 (568) player positions (games), 8,504 (562) opponent positions; 237 player resignations in this cell
findings.caveat: Played-out games are selected; positions weighted per position.

findings.section: 6. Rule of thumb in engine terms
findings.claim: In rapid, positions at -1000..-500 scored 0.27 when the player played them out, nearly three times what they scored for the opponents; over half of the player's rapid resignations fall in this eval band.
findings.metric: observed score of positions in the side's played-out games with engine eval -1000..-500 from that side's view; CIs clustered by game
findings.n: 1,297 (125) player positions (games), 2,326 (149) opponent positions; 87 player resignations in this cell
findings.caveat: Rapid has few games; played-out games are selected.

findings.section: 5. 'Had to go' vs 'gave up'
findings.claim: About a quarter of the player's resignations came from still-playable positions (model P(win) >= 0.2) and these carry 65% of the total cost; the opponents' share of such resignations is lower.
findings.metric: share of the side's resignations with model P(win) >= 0.2 from the resigner's view; cost is the played-out valuation summed over the class
findings.stake_note: Played-out cost of the player's 203 still-playable resignations; 65% of the 131 points all resignations cost (opponents' still-playable resignations: 71.6 points).
findings.caveat: Class boundaries use the model-relative P(win).

findings.section: 5. 'Had to go' vs 'gave up'
findings.claim: A quarter of the player's resignations came from clearly lost positions (model P(win) < 0.05) and these cost almost nothing; the opponents resign from clearly lost positions much more often.
findings.metric: share of the side's resignations with model P(win) < 0.05 from the resigner's view; cost is the played-out valuation summed over the class
findings.stake_note: Played-out cost of the player's 206 clearly lost resignations; 3% of the total cost (opponents' clearly lost resignations: 2.8 points).
findings.caveat: Class boundaries use the model-relative P(win).

findings.section: 5. 'Had to go' vs 'gave up'
findings.claim: Nearly half of the player's resignations came from nearly lost positions (model P(win) 0.05-0.2), which carry about a third of the total cost.
findings.metric: share of the side's resignations with model P(win) 0.05-0.2 from the resigner's view; cost is the played-out valuation summed over the class
findings.stake_note: Played-out cost of the player's 379 nearly lost resignations (opponents' nearly lost resignations: 22.2 points).
findings.caveat: Class boundaries use the model-relative P(win).

findings.section: 5. 'Had to go' vs 'gave up'
findings.claim: When resigning from still-playable positions both sides had about four fifths of the base time left on the clock.
findings.metric: mean resigner's clock as a fraction of the base time at still-playable (P(win) >= 0.2) resignations
findings.caveat: Clock at the position after the last recorded move.

findings.section: 5. 'Had to go' vs 'gave up'
findings.claim: A third of still-playable resignations, for both sides, followed a quick last own move (at or below the resigner's median move time in that game).
findings.metric: share of still-playable (P(win) >= 0.2) resignations whose last own move took at most the resigner's median move time in that game
findings.caveat: 'Quick last move' refers to the resigner's last own move, not the resignation itself, whose timing is not recorded.

findings.section: 5. 'Had to go' vs 'gave up'
findings.claim: Nearly half of the player's still-playable resignations were the last game of a session, against about a third of the nearly lost ones.
findings.metric: share of the player's still-playable (P(win) >= 0.2) resignations that were the last game of the session; nearly lost class: 0.32 [0.28, 0.37], clearly lost: 0.39 [0.33, 0.46]
findings.caveat: Opponents' sessions are unknown; a session ended by quitting in frustration looks the same as one ended by an interruption.

findings.section: 5. 'Had to go' vs 'gave up'
findings.claim: 65 of the player's 788 resignations (8%) fit the 'had to go' pattern: still playable, at least 25% of the clock left and a quick last own move; they cost 28.7 points on the played-out valuation.
findings.metric: share of the player's resignations that are still playable (P(win) >= 0.2) with resigner's clock >= 25% of base and a quick last own move
findings.stake_note: Played-out valuation summed over the 65 'had to go' resignations; the other 138 still-playable resignations (low clock or slow last move) cost 56.1 points.
findings.caveat: 'Had to go' is a proxy; if these were real interruptions there is nothing to change.

findings.section: 5. 'Had to go' vs 'gave up'
findings.claim: The 'had to go' resignations were the last game of a session more often than the player's clearly or nearly lost resignations.
findings.metric: share of resignations that were the last game of the session, 'had to go' resignations minus clearly/nearly lost resignations (35% [31%, 39%]); 38% of all the player's resignations were last games
findings.n: 65 'had to go' resignations vs 585 clearly/nearly lost
findings.caveat: The last-game-of-session marker cannot distinguish an interruption from quitting in frustration after the resignation.

findings.section: 5. 'Had to go' vs 'gave up'
findings.claim: In bullet about one resignation in seven followed straight after the resigner's own blunder (last own move cost >= 0.2 expected points), for both sides.
findings.metric: share of the side's resignations whose last own move had ep_loss >= 0.2

findings.section: 5. 'Had to go' vs 'gave up'
findings.claim: In blitz about one resignation in seven followed straight after the resigner's own blunder, for both sides.
findings.metric: share of the side's resignations whose last own move had ep_loss >= 0.2

findings.section: 5. 'Had to go' vs 'gave up'
findings.claim: In rapid about one resignation in seven followed straight after the resigner's own blunder, for both sides.
findings.metric: share of the side's resignations whose last own move had ep_loss >= 0.2
